sn35.121:1.1: On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthı̄ in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park.
sn35.121:1.2: Then, while the Blessed One was alone in seclusion, a reflection arose in his mind thus:
sn35.121:1.3: “The states that ripen in liberation have come to maturity in Rāhula.
sn35.121:1.4: Let me lead him on further to the destruction of the taints.”
sn35.121:1.5: Then, in the morning, the Blessed One dressed and, taking bowl and robe, walked for alms in Sāvatthı̄.
sn35.121:1.6: When he had returned from the alms round, after his meal he addressed the Venerable Rāhula thus:
sn35.121:1.8: Let us go to the Blind Men’s Grove for the day’s abiding.”
sn35.121:1.9: “Yes, venerable sir,” the Venerable Rāhula replied and, having taken a sitting cloth, he followed close behind the Blessed One.
sn35.121:2.1: Now on that occasion many thousands of devatās followed the Blessed One, thinking:
sn35.121:2.2: “Today the Blessed One will lead the Venerable Rāhula on further to the destruction of the taints.”
sn35.121:2.3: Then the Blessed One plunged into the Blind Men’s Grove and sat down at the foot of a certain tree on a seat that was prepared for him.
sn35.121:2.4: The Venerable Rāhula paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side.
sn35.121:2.5: The Blessed One then said to him:
sn35.121:3.1: “What do you think, Rāhula, is the eye permanent or impermanent?”
sn35.121:5.1: –“Is what is impermanent suffering or happiness?”
sn35.121:7.1: –“Is what is impermanent, suffering, and subject to change fit to be regarded thus:
sn35.121:7.2: ‘This is mine, this I am, this is my self’?”
sn35.121:9.1: “Are forms permanent or impermanent? … Is eye-consciousness … Is eye-contact …
sn35.121:15.1: Is anything included in feeling, perception, volitional formations, and consciousness arisen with eye-contact as condition permanent or impermanent?”
sn35.121:16.1: –“Impermanent, venerable sir.” (The rest as in the preceding paragraph. )
sn35.121:45.1: Is anything included in feeling, perception, volitional formations, and consciousness arisen with mind-contact as condition permanent or impermanent?”
sn35.121:47.1: –“Is what is impermanent suffering or happiness?”
sn35.121:49.1: –“Is what is impermanent, suffering, and subject to change fit to be regarded thus:
sn35.121:49.2: ‘This is mine, this I am, this is my self’?”
sn35.121:51.1: “Seeing thus, Rāhula, the instructed noble disciple experiences revulsion towards the eye, revulsion towards forms, revulsion towards eye-consciousness, revulsion towards eye-contact; revulsion towards anything included in feeling, perception, volitional formations, and consciousness arisen with eye-contact as condition.
sn35.121:51.2: He experiences revulsion towards the ear … towards the mind …
sn35.121:52.1: towards anything included in feeling, perception, volitional formations, and consciousness arisen with mind-contact as condition.
sn35.121:52.2: “Experiencing revulsion, he becomes dispassionate. Through dispassion [his mind] is liberated. When it is liberated there comes the knowledge: ‘It’s liberated.’
sn35.121:52.3: He understands: ‘Destroyed is birth, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more for this state of being.’ ”
sn35.121:53.1: This is what the Blessed One said.
sn35.121:53.2: Elated, the Venerable Rāhula delighted in the Blessed One’s statement.
sn35.121:53.3: And while this discourse was being spoken, the Venerable Rāhula’s mind was liberated from the taints by nonclinging,
sn35.121:53.4: and in those many thousands of devatās there arose the dust-free, stainless vision of the Dhamma:
sn35.121:53.5: “Whatever is subject to origination is all subject to cessation.”
